provider_evidence_records.field_family: S&P DJI S&P 500 benchmark methodology, index level publication, price / total / net total return variants, and benchmark-data candidate evidence.

evidence_source_refs.evidence_note: WebFetched on 2026-05-28 at https://www.spglobal.com/spdji/en/indices/equity/sp-500/. Official index page identifies the S&P 500 as a US large-cap index and provides official methodology, factsheet, and index documentation links. This is benchmark identity and methodology evidence only, not proof of project-ready licensed historical return access.

WebFetched on 2026-05-28 at https://www.spglobal.com/spdji/en/methodology/article/sp-us-indices-methodology/. Official methodology page and PDF cover S&P U.S. index construction and index-value publication framing. This supports future benchmark packet review but does not supply a local historical total-return series.

evidence_source_refs.source_title: S&P Dow Jones Indices Index Mathematics Methodology
evidence_source_refs.evidence_note: WebFetched on 2026-05-28 at https://www.spglobal.com/spdji/en/methodology/article/index-mathematics-methodology/. Official methodology documents return-type calculation concepts including price return, total return, and net total return methodology. This is construction evidence, not an authorization to store or redistribute index history.

missing_required_evidence: Licensed or otherwise permitted historical S&P 500 price-return, total-return, or net-total-return series source with date range, currency, unit, and update schedule.
Data-access path, API/table name, request parameters, fetch timestamp, and no-zero-fill missing-session policy.
Storage, redistribution, non-display, derived-report, and private research permission for local project artifacts.
Membership history source and PIT limitations if S&P 500 constituents are used for attribution rather than only return comparison.
limitations: Official methodology and index pages are not a substitute for a reviewed historical benchmark data feed.
ETF proxies such as SPY may remain fallback candidates, but this record is direct-index-source evidence and does not approve proxy substitution.

provider_evidence_records.field_family: Nasdaq-100 benchmark methodology, official index dissemination surfaces, and Nasdaq 100 benchmark-data candidate evidence.

evidence_source_refs.evidence_note: WebFetched on 2026-05-28 at https://indexes.nasdaq.com/docs/Methodology_NDX.pdf. Official methodology describes Nasdaq-100 index eligibility, constituent selection, maintenance, and where index values / weights are available through Nasdaq index dissemination products. This is methodology and distribution-surface evidence only.

WebFetched on 2026-05-28 at https://indexes.nasdaqomx.com/Index/Overview/NDX. Official index page provides Nasdaq-100 overview, performance display, factsheet, and methodology links. Displayed performance does not by itself create a local, licensed, historical total-return feed.

missing_required_evidence: Licensed historical Nasdaq-100 price-return, total-return, or selected benchmark-return series with exact ticker/index identifiers.
Data-access mechanism for local monthly return reconstruction, including missing sessions and timezone alignment.
Authorization for local storage, derived private reports, and benchmark-sensitive evidence publication inside this private repo.
Rule for using QQQ as a sensitivity proxy when direct Nasdaq-100 total-return data is not available or not licensed.
limitations: Nasdaq methodology and index pages support future benchmark evidence review but do not authorize provider selection or data fetch.
The artifact does not decide whether Nasdaq 100, QQQ, or sector ETF sensitivity is the final benchmark path for any lane.

provider_evidence_records.field_family: FTSE Russell / LSEG Russell US Indexes methodology, Russell 1000 benchmark identity, construction, reconstitution, and benchmark-data candidate evidence.

evidence_source_refs.evidence_note: WebFetched on 2026-05-28 at https://www.lseg.com/en/ftse-russell/indices/russell-us. Official LSEG page describes the Russell US index family and provides methodology / ground-rules links plus Russell 1000 product context. This is benchmark identity and documentation evidence.

evidence_source_refs.source_title: Russell US Indexes Construction and Methodology
evidence_source_refs.evidence_note: WebFetched on 2026-05-28 at https://www.lseg.com/content/dam/ftse-russell/en_us/documents/ground-rules/russell-us-indexes-construction-and-methodology.pdf. Official ground rules define Russell US index construction, market-cap ranking, reconstitution, and Russell 1000 / 2000 / 3000 family mechanics. This does not prove local access to historical return files.

WebFetched on 2026-05-28 at https://www.lseg.com/en/media-centre/press-releases/ftse-russell/2026/russell-reconstitution-2026-schedule. Official release records the 2026 Russell US Indexes reconstitution schedule, rank day, preliminary membership list timing, final close, and semi-annual 2026 framing. This supports reconstitution-awareness review, not backfilled index-return data.

missing_required_evidence: Licensed historical Russell 1000 return series, return type, currency, unit, frequency, and delivery path.
Exact treatment for price return vs total return and any net-of-tax variant if used.
Calendar, missing-session, and no-zero-fill rules aligned to US lane monthly evidence windows.
Membership history access and license if Russell constituents are used for universe overlap or attribution.
limitations: Russell 1000 remains the provisional US-long and US-short primary benchmark, but this artifact does not finalize ship-gate benchmark selection.
Methodology and reconstitution evidence is not sufficient for a project-ready historical return feed.

provider_evidence_records.field_family: GICS taxonomy methodology and S&P Global / MSCI GICS history product candidate evidence for issuer-level industry membership reconstruction.

evidence_source_refs.evidence_note: WebFetched on 2026-05-28 at https://www.msci.com/our-solutions/indexes/gics. Official MSCI page describes GICS as a jointly developed four-tier global classification framework with annual methodology review. This proves taxonomy owner/methodology context, not project-ready issuer-level PIT history.

evidence_source_refs.source_title: S&P Dow Jones Indices GICS Topic Page
evidence_source_refs.evidence_note: WebFetched on 2026-05-28 at https://www.spglobal.com/spdji/en/landing/topic/gics/. Official S&P DJI page routes to the GICS methodology and related documents. This is taxonomy methodology evidence only.

evidence_source_refs.source_title: S&P Global Differentiated Data GICS Direct And GICS History
evidence_source_refs.evidence_note: WebFetched on 2026-05-28 at https://www.spglobal.com/market-intelligence/en/solutions/differentiated-data. Official S&P Global page describes GICS Direct and GICS History concepts, including historical company-level GICS codes, descriptions, company names, and identifiers. This is a candidate source, not an approved licensed feed.

WebFetched on 2026-05-28 at https://www.spglobal.com/marketintelligence/en/documents/gics-history-brochure.pdf. Official brochure describes historical company-level GICS classification data, company identifiers, coverage, and delivery options. This supports future PIT membership review but still requires license, data dictionary, sample rows, effective-date semantics, and universe coverage evidence.

missing_required_evidence: Issuer-level PIT GICS membership history with effective dates, company identifiers, issuer/security mapping, and row-level sample validation.
License and local-storage permission for GICS history, derived reports, industry-normalization outputs, and private research artifacts.
Coverage counts for the US-long and US-short universes, including inactive / delisted issuers and identifier changes.
Explicit as-of eligibility rule for using classification changes in backtests and live-normalized evidence windows.
limitations: GICS methodology alone is not issuer-level PIT membership evidence.
The GICS History product is a candidate source, but this artifact does not obtain a sample, license, or data dictionary and therefore keeps US-long industry normalization blocked.
